defects.claim_says: first end 1977-10-19, Executive Order 12014 deletion of section 8; 'the held order [EO 10979] does not say that it ended this paragraph'
defects.source_says: EO 10979 (Dec. 12, 1961, 26 FR 11937) ordered EO 10717 'be amended by substituting for section 2, 7, and 8 thereof the following'; the substituted section 8 contains no paragraphs (a) or (b) (the 8(a) standard moved into new section 2(b); a different ineligibility sentence replaced 8(b)). Substituting the whole section removed original 8(a) and 8(b) on 1961-12-12, so by 1977 section 8 held no such paragraphs and EO 12014 could not first end them. The claim itself says EO 10979 restated section 8 'without the enumerated criteria'. Earlier end missed; date, actor and mechanism wrong for both clauses.

defects.claim_says: The U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 4504 ... prints Executive Order 10717 as amended ... with this section in its original wording
defects.source_says: Section 2 was replaced by EO 10979; the clause's own judgment_reason says 'The restated section 2 is printed in the current U.S. Code note'. The legal basis is false for section 2 and internally inconsistent.

defects.claim_says: Clause operative; 'read as continuing in amended form through the chairman and invitation sentences'; current predicate: 'this clause is carried forward in the restated text as stated in its reason'
defects.source_says: The clause span (EO_11858.txt chars 1486-2169) also contains the lead-in of section 1(b): 'The Committee shall have primary continuing responsibility within the Executive Branch for monitoring the impact of foreign investment ... and for coordinating the implementation of United States policy on such investment.' The claim decides that command nowhere: the reason for sec1-6 does not mention it, while the four 1(b) item clauses say EO 13456 sec. 1 'replaced this paragraph' and nothing in the restated text carries the paragraph forward (ended 2008-01-23). An operative command inside an operative clause is thus left undecided and contradicts the claim's own treatment of paragraph 1(b).
